column386: text_preview
Ciao to you too.
It’s good to see you.
I've actually been looking forward to this all week.
I had a couple of those 'aha' moments while I was out hiking, and I'm kind of excited to unpack them.
But yeah, how have you been?
Has it been a good week?
Ciao to you too.
It’s good to see you.
I've actually been looking forward to this all week.
I had a couple of those 'aha' moments while I was out hiking, and I'm kind of excited to unpack them.
But yeah, how have you been?
Has it been a good week?
I'm doing pretty well.
It was a... mixed week.
I had that great hike I mentioned, but also a ridiculously frustrating day at work that, weirdly, led to one of those 'aha' moments.
So, yeah, I'm definitely ready to unpack some of that whenever you are.
No worries at all, I'm sure you've got a lot of names swimming around in your head.
For a second there, I thought maybe I'd said something so wild last week you had to block me out.
But yeah, it's Alex.
Glad we're all good.
Yeah, it was... exactly what I needed.
There's something about getting up high enough to see the whole valley, feeling the wind and just the quiet... it really puts my ridiculous work drama into perspective.
It's like my brain finally has room to breathe, you know?
And it actually connected to that frustrating thing at work in a way I wasn't expecting.
Yeah, so... the work thing.
It was this project I've been pouring a lot of myself into, and a senior colleague just... well, he basically steamrolled my part of it in a big meeting.
He presented my ideas as a footnote to his own.
It was just so frustrating, you know?
For a day or two, I was just stewing in it, feeling really small and kind of... invisible.
And that's the feeling that I think I finally got some perspective on during that hike.
I'm a UX designer.
So I work on the user experience for software and apps... trying to make them not-terrible to use, basically.
And honestly, I usually love it.
But it's moments like that one last week that make you question it, you know?
It's hard to feel good about your work when someone can just... absorb it, and act like you just added a few decorative touches.
It's just... incredibly frustrating.
What makes me feel good?
It's when you actually solve a problem for a real person.
You know, you watch a user test and you can see the moment something just... clicks for them.
When you've taken this messy, complicated thing and made it intuitive and simple.
That's the whole point, right?
To actually help someone not want to throw their computer out the window.
It's just... that feeling is what makes the other stuff, the politics and the egos, so much more infuriating.
Yeah, that's a good way to put it.
I guess I'm on a mission to save the world from wanting to throw their devices out the window.
But it's more than just helping, it's...
I don't know, it's about making something that just for someone.
Taking a frustration and smoothing it out.
It's a really good feeling, seeing that click happen for them.
I think I am, actually.
I'm definitely the planner in my friend group.
I'm the one who's like, "Okay, if we want to go on this trip, here are three good options for an Airbnb, and I've already checked the transit routes."
It's that same impulse, I guess.
I just want to make sure everyone's having a good time and that the experience is... seamless.
It feels good to take care of my people, you know?
The great unsolved problem, right?
I mean, I want that partnership... that feeling of taking care of someone and having them take care of you.
It's just... honestly, after the week I've had, the thought of navigating another person's ego and... all that stuff... it just feels exhausting.
It's hard enough at work, you know?
No, not right now.
The... position is currently vacant, you could say.
I really do want that... that partnership, someone to build something with.
But honestly, after the week I've had, the idea of swiping and making all that small talk... it just sounds so draining.
It feels like I'm already managing enough personalities just to get through my workday.
I don't really see myself as an angry person.
Like with that whole thing at work last week, I wasn't really angry, just... gutted, you know?
With a partner, I imagine it would be the same, only magnified.
It would probably feel less like anger and more like a profound sadness.
Like, a betrayal of that trust.
The feeling that the one person who's supposed to see you... doesn't.
That would hurt more than anything else.
That's a good question.
I've always felt like I have a pretty solid sense of who I am.
I think a lot of that comes from my parents, you know?
They were always just... a really steady, supportive foundation to build on.
But it's funny you ask that now.
After this week, feeling so... invisible at work... it does make you wobble a bit.
It feels like this core part of me, the part that's competent and helpful, just got... erased.
And that's a really heavy feeling.
It makes you wonder how solid anything is, really.
Well... my first instinct is usually to get busy.
To... reconnect, I guess.
I'll reach out to my friends, try to make a plan.
It helps remind me that I'm... seen, you know?
That I actually have a place.
Or I'll just get outside, go for a run or something.
It's like I need to physically feel my feet on the ground to remember that I'm still here, still solid.
It’s a really lonely feeling, otherwise.
Like being a ghost in your own life.
Oh, no, nothing like that.
My record's pretty clean, I think.
I've always been pretty... even-keeled, you know?
This past week has been the first time I've really felt... well, completely knocked sideways by something.
It's a new and not-so-fun feeling.
I've never really connected those dots before.
I mean, I don't know if there's a specific... cultural mandate for being even-keeled, but my family is definitely of the 'keep calm and carry on' variety.
So, yeah... maybe it is?
It's interesting to think about.
It certainly didn't prepare me for feeling... well, completely flattened like I did this week.
That felt like a whole different planet.
My brain decided to host an all-night marathon of What You Should Have Said,' which isn't exactly a recipe for a good night's sleep.
I'd just lie there, feeling... heavy, you know?
Like my body was totally exhausted from the week, but my mind just refused to clock out.
It was pretty frustrating, honestly.
The future... well, a week ago I would've had a much clearer answer.
Right now, I just...
I hope I'm in a place where I feel seen.
Where the work I do, the effort I put in, is actually acknowledged.
I guess I hope that extends to my personal life, too.
To eventually have a partner who... who really sees me.
The thought of that feels really nice, but also... a little terrifying after this week, if I'm being honest.
That's a really good question.
The fear of being judged by others is definitely what kicked all this off at work.
That feeling of being...
I don't know, scanned and then dismissed.
But the self-judgment, that's the part that feels... heavier.
That's the voice that replays everything at night.
It feels more personal, somehow, and a lot harder to argue with.
I guess I was.
I always did the work, got good grades.
It was just... what you did, you know?
But I don't think this is about not being used to failure.
I mean, I've messed things up before, everyone does.
This... this feels different.
This doesn't feel like failed... it feels like I was failed.
Like I was just... completely disregarded.
And maybe... maybe I'm not used to that feeling.
It's a lot harder to fix.
Just hit the big three-oh a couple of months ago, actually.
It's funny... you'd think by thirty you'd be a bit more...
I don't know, bulletproof?
But this week has made me feel about fifteen all over again.
Definitely not the solid, got-it-all-figured-out vibe I was expecting from this decade.
I'd really like that.
This feeling has been... pretty heavy, and I don't really want to just carry it around all week by myself.
Let's definitely continue next week.
It... it helps, just talking about it.
That feeling we talked about last week, that heaviness... it's definitely still been hanging around.
It's maybe less of a sharp shock now and more of a... a dull ache.
And honestly, it's still just so frustrating when I think about it.
I'm ready to get into it today.
It's... yeah, it's still not great.
I'm falling asleep okay, but I keep waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning with this... jolt.
My heart will be pounding, and my brain just starts replaying everything from that day at work.
It's like my body is still on high alert, even when I'm supposed to be resting.
It's just... really draining.
I mean, I try.
I try to do the deep breathing thing, you know?
In through the nose, out through the mouth.
But it's hard to convince my body to calm down when my heart feels like it's trying to hammer its way out of my chest.
Sometimes I'll get up and get a glass of water, just to... change my physical state.
It kinda helps, sometimes.
But mostly, I just feel like I have to wait for the wave to pass.
Yeah, a little bit.
I've mentioned that work has been... a lot.
But I haven't really gotten into the specifics of it, the whole credit-stealing thing.
I don't know, it feels so... heavy to just drop on them.
I'm usually the one organizing the fun stuff, you know?
It feels weird to be the one bringing the storm cloud to the picnic.
I don't want to be a burden.
Well, I haven't really given them the chance to understand, to be honest.
I've kept it pretty surface-level.
It feels... it's hard to explain that feeling of being completely gutted by something at work without feeling like you're just dumping it all on them.
I guess I'm afraid they won't really get it, or they'll see me differently.
I don't want to be the person who brings the mood down.
Oh, I mean, it's usually the best.
That's my element, right?
I feel relaxed, I feel like myself.
I feel a little on guard, almost.
Like I'm there, but I'm also holding a piece of myself back.
I'm trying so hard not to let this work thing poison the well, you know?
It's just... annoying that I can't even fully relax with them right now.
My head knows that, and you're right.
But it’s not really about doubting them, I guess.
It’s more… I’m afraid of changing the dynamic.
I don’t want their first thought when they see me to be, 'Oh, I wonder how that awful work thing is going.'
I just want to be their fun friend, you know?
And I feel like I'm losing that part of myself right now.
Yeah, I hope that part is just in a corner.
It feels... pretty far away right now.
And my parents... no, I haven't really talked to them about this.
Our relationship is great, we're really close.
But I think that's almost why it's harder.
I don't want to worry them, you know?
They see me as so steady and capable.
I guess I don't want to show them this... flattened version of me.
Oh, she's... she's wonderful.
The most supportive person you could ever meet.
That's kind of the problem, though.
If I told her how gutted I've been feeling, she'd go into full-on mama bear mode, and I just...
I can't handle that right now.
It makes me angry just thinking about having to re-live it for her.
I don't want to see her worried, and I don't want her trying to fix something she can't.
My dad... he's great, too.
He's just... he's the fixer.
His immediate response would be, "Okay, what's the plan?
What are the action steps?"
And there aren't any, not really.
So then I'd just be... presenting him with a problem he can't solve.
I think seeing him feel powerless on my behalf would almost be worse.
It feels like I'd just be letting him down.
It's just... a weird kind of loneliness, isn't it?
To have people you're so close to, but to feel like you have to...
I don't know, protect them from your own reality.
It almost makes the whole thing feel heavier.
Like this is my problem to figure out, and mine alone.
Yeah, I think that's the word for it.
It's a weird brand of lonely, though.
It’s not like I’m actually alone, but it feels like… I don’t know, like I’m standing on the other side of a soundproof window.
I can see everyone, but I can’t quite connect.
It’s like this whole thing from work put a wall up, and I’m the only one on this side of it.
I guess I haven't really thought about it in those terms.
It's not like there are any, you know, grand family traditions about suffering in silence.
But... the culture of ?
Yeah, I think so.
There's this unspoken rule, you know?
Don't be a burden.
It feels like a very... fundamental part of how we show love, by not making the other person worry.
I was born and raised just outside of Boston.
So, not exactly a different country or anything, but... yeah, thinking about it now, that whole stoic, 'pull yourself up by your bootstraps' New England thing is definitely part of the air there.
It's not just my family, it feels like the whole environment I grew up in.
And it just... it makes this whole thing from work feel like a personal failing I'm supposed to just handle on my own, quietly.
I guess so, yeah.
I mean, my childhood was pretty calm, all things considered.
I think the main objective was always... to be easy.
Don't cause a fuss, don't make waves.
It was less about being bad or good and more about just... not being a problem to solve.
It definitely feels like an early version of that "don't be a burden" thing we were just talking about.
Well, that's... a very direct question.
I guess I don't really think about it in those terms, you know?
The "good girl" thing we just talked about... that box never really felt like it fit right.
Does that make sense?
It feels like trying to answer that just creates another problem to solve, and I've had enough of that lately.
We're really... drilling down on this one, huh?
I guess the honest answer is I don't really have a neat label for it.
The words, 'girl,' 'boy'... they just feel like someone else's boxes, you know?
Like another set of expectations.
And honestly, after everything at work, the thought of having one more category I could fail at performing correctly... it's just exhausting.
I'm just trying to be Alex, and that feels like enough of a job right now.
Is that how I'm coming across today?
I guess after that last conversation I do feel a little... world-weary.
But no, definitely thirty.
I'm... a little confused, where did you get that from?
Oh, hey, it's okay.
It just... it really threw me for a loop for a second there.
I was starting to wonder if I was having one of those weeks where I'd aged twenty years without noticing.
But yeah, we're good.
It was just a weird moment.
I'll definitely try on the sleep front.
It's always a bit of an adventure, you know?
But thanks, this was good.
You have a good week too, and I'll see you next time.
I'm doing alright, thanks.
It's been one of those weeks where you feel like you're running in five different directions at once.
I've actually been thinking a lot about our last conversation, about that pressure to always be... capable.
It's been popping up in some interesting, and kind of annoying, places.
So yeah, I'm curious to dig into that a bit more, if that works.
I mean, I can just picture it now... he'd probably try to workshop my dating app profile or create a flowchart for first dates.
It's just... that's exactly the kind of thing that doesn't have a "concrete solution," you know?
It would just make him feel helpless and me feel like a project that's failing.
My mom... yeah, that's different.
I mean, I , technically.
She's not a fixer like he is, she's more... a worrier.
And honestly, that's almost its own kind of pressure.
It feels like I'd be giving her the edited version, you know?
I'd have to sand down all the rough or... messy edges so she doesn't lose sleep over it.
It just feels like I'd be managing her feelings instead of talking about my own.
I've been... you know, swiping.
Doing the whole app thing.
But it's felt a little... hollow, I guess?
After that whole thing at work, my... my armor feels a bit thin, you know?
The idea of putting myself out there for more potential judgment just feels... exhausting.
It's hard to be open to connection when you're mostly just feeling the need to protect yourself.
I think... if I was married, we'd probably be having a very different kind of conversation.
We'd be way past the 'swiping on apps is exhausting' phase, I'd hope.
No, I'm... very much single.
"Suffer"... that feels like a big word, but I guess it's not wrong.
The... the initial shock has passed, but the heaviness is definitely still there.
It's like this constant, low-grade static in the back of my head.
And my sleep is still... yeah, it's still a mess.
So it's not as sharp, maybe, but it feels like it's settled in.
I don't know if it's that they're not ...
I think they are, or they're trying to be.
It's more that... this feeling is so new to me, it's hard to explain it in a way they can really grasp.
But to answer your question... no, it hasn't always been like this at all.
Growing up, my family was... that was my safe place.
I could absolutely be vulnerable.
I remember being a kid and just, you know, having a total meltdown over something silly, and it was... it was fine.
It was just accepted.
It feels a lot more complicated to do that now.
Bring back that kid...
I mean, I'd love to.
He was a lot less worried about what everyone thought, that's for sure.
It's a nice idea.
I don't know, a bit like trying to put the genie back in the bottle, but in reverse?
The world just seems so much bigger and more complicated now.
How do you even begin to do that when you're... well, me, and not nine years old?
I'd wake up, and the first thing on my mind would be what cartoon was on, not... this.
I'd go to school, and the biggest political drama was, like, who you sat with at lunch.
After school, I'd just get on my bike and ride around the neighborhood for hours until my mom yelled out the door for dinner.
There was no... performance.
No worrying about how I was coming across to people.
It all just... was.
It feels like a different person, honestly.
Yeah... yeah, I do.
It's one of the few things that's stuck around, I guess.
It’s just... it's not the same feeling.
It's not that 'ride until you're called in for dinner' freedom.
Now it's more like... maintenance.
Good maintenance, for my head, but still... something I have to schedule.
The simplicity is gone.
Just ride with no real destination.
It sounds nice, actually.
As for the future... whew.
That question feels a lot bigger than it did a few weeks ago.
Honestly, right now I'm just trying to feel... solid again.
The future feels a little out of focus until I can get my own feet back under me, you know?
It’s still pretty broken up.
I’ll be fine when I first go to bed, but then I wake up around, like, two or three in the morning and my brain just… clicks on.
It’s like it’s trying to solve a puzzle that's already finished, just replaying everything from... well, from that whole situation at work.
It’s hard to get back to sleep after that.
Yeah, uh, we went out for a bit on Saturday.
It was... it was fine.
Good to see them.
But I felt a little bit like I was watching a movie of us hanging out, instead of actually there.
I just kept the conversation light, you know, played my usual part.
I don't know, risky, to bring up the work stuff.
I don't want to change the vibe for everyone.
I don't know if they'd do it on purpose, you know?
It's not like they'd be mean about it.
But... yeah, I think it would change things.
I'd become 'the one going through it.'
And then I'm not just a friend anymore, I'm... a project.
Or someone they have to check in on.
It just changes my... my role.
And I don't want to be the guy who brings the whole vibe down.
It feels safer to just... keep playing my part.
It's not an angry feeling, it's just... it feels like the same thing we were just talking about, you know?
If I pick a label, then there’s a whole script that comes with it, and a whole audience that expects me to perform it correctly.
It’s just… it feels like another pressure to be a certain way, and I already feel like I’m juggling a lot of those.
I guess the label was just...'student.'
And the pressure was all about being a one.
It's not like with friends, it felt... more official?
Like your performance was constantly being graded, and that grade defined you.
If you weren't hitting the mark, you weren't just struggling, you a failure.
It feels like the same kind of trap, just... a different box.
I studied English Literature.
I really did love it, you know, the actual reading and the ideas.
But it was kind of a perfect storm for that pressure we were just talking about.
It’s so subjective, so every essay felt less like an assignment and more like… a verdict on how my mind works.
It just made that whole fear of being a 'failure' feel incredibly personal.
Hmm... no, I don't think that's the right word.
It wasn't really a hot feeling, you know?
It was more... cold.
The verdict was in, and there was no one to yell at.
It felt less like something to fight against and more like a quiet, crushing fact.
It's more deflating than anything... just, yeah, flattening.
My sense of self...
I mean, on the inside, it feels pretty consistent?
Like, I know who I am when I wake up.
But trying to... describe it, to put a label on it for you... it feels like that same pressure we were just talking about.
It feels like I'm supposed to give a 'right' answer, and honestly, I'm just... tired of being graded.
It feels like another box.
Logically, I get that.
It's just, my brain is so conditioned to hunt for the rubric, you know?
To try and figure out what the 'A' answer is.
It's a hard habit to break.
It's that same... heaviness I mentioned, I guess.
This feeling that I'm being evaluated, even when I'm not.
Yeah... "just live freely."
It sounds so simple, but my brain immediately starts looking for the catch.
Like, what are the parameters for 'freely'?
Is there a right way to do it?
But I hear you.
The idea of just… getting on the bike, no goal, just movement… it sounds nice.
I’ll try to just… not ask for a report card at the end of the ride.
Hey, good to see you.
So, I took your advice from last week.
I did the whole "just live freely" thing, went on that bike ride... and it was... interesting.
It was definitely part of a pretty mixed week, a real mix of highs and lows.
I'm actually kinda eager to unpack some of it today, if that's cool.
I think I might have had one of those "aha" moments we've talked about.
So... it was after that work event I mentioned, where I just felt so... scrutinized.
And then a couple of days later I was out on that hike, and it was just... quiet.
Just the sound of my feet on the trail.
That feeling of being graded, that heaviness?
I realized I'm the one carrying the clipboard.
It's not just other people, it's .
I'm the one who's constantly evaluating everything I do.
How did I feel...
For a second, all the noise from that work thing just... stopped.
And then it was this weird mix of relief and... God, I don't know, a little bit of dread?
It felt freeing, to realize I could just put the clipboard down.
But it was also heavy, knowing I was the one who picked it up in the first place.
It wasn't exactly a happy feeling, but it felt... true.
I don't know if that's what I was doing, really.
It was more like...
I just let it happen?
I didn't try to fight the dread or hold onto the relief.
I just kept walking and kinda let them both sit there next to each other.
It's a little infuriating, honestly, to have that big realization and then just... keep walking.
It feels like I should have gotten a certificate or something.
Did they meet... huh.
No, I don't think they really .
It was more like they were suddenly on opposite sides of the same room, having a bit of a staredown.
They're definitely aware of each other.
But one isn't going to leave just because the other is there, you know?
It's... a little irritating, actually.
A standoff, and I'm just kind of stuck in the middle of it.
I don't think they'd do it.
Like one of those awkward, mandated team-building exercises.
They'd touch hands for a second, maybe, but they'd both be looking at me like, 'Are you serious with this?'
It just feels... dishonest, somehow.
And it makes the whole thing feel even heavier, you know?
Like I'm trying to pretend the problem isn't there.
"Pretending" is a good word for it.
I saw them over the weekend, and it's just... exhausting.
It feels like I'm broadcasting on 'Everything's Fine FM' and I'm the only one who knows it's all pre-recorded.
I can feel myself watching them, scanning, trying to make sure I’m hitting my cues as the 'fun friend'.
It’s a lot of work to keep that show on the road.
My mom and dad... they're great.
But... it's kind of the same thing as with my friends, just a different station.
I can't really... be fully honest about all this.
Especially with my mom.
If I even hint at how heavy things feel, she just... she worries so much, and then I end up spending all my energy managing her anxiety.
It's just easier to keep up the pretense that everything's fine.
It makes me feel even more... alone with it, somehow.
No, it's... it's still the same job.
But it doesn't feel the same, you know?
It's like... the volume's been turned down on all the good parts.
Ever since that whole thing happened, it just feels... heavy.
I'm still doing the work, but it's hard to find that... that drive I used to have.
It's like I'm just going through the motions.
Oh, um... it's a new project on user experience, actually.
Mapping out a... a whole new customer journey to make everything feel more intuitive.
It’s the kind of puzzle I usually love to solve.
But I don't know, it's been hard to really sink my teeth into it.
I'm going through the motions, doing the work, but that feeling of... really getting lost in it, you know?
It's just... not there right now.
Yeah, but... it’s not really at the work.
It’s more... an internal thing.
Like, I’ll hit a snag in this new UX mapping, something that normally I'd find interesting to solve, and there's just this flash of... intense irritation.
It's aimed at myself, I think.
Like, 'why can't you just focus?'
It's a hot, frustrating feeling, but it burns out fast and just leaves me feeling... heavy.
And even more stuck than before.
It’s like my brain’s favorite late-night show.
It’s not even necessarily big things I did , it’s just… a highlight reel of that whole situation.
Wondering if I should’ve said something different, or… I don't know, just handled it with more… something.
It's infuriating, honestly, because it’s so unproductive.
There are definitely better things to be thinking about in bed.
Yeah, that's the fun part.
I'll lie there, completely exhausted, but my brain just refuses to get the memo.
It's like it's running on a different power source, just replaying that... that whole work situation.
I just want to switch it off, you know?
But it just keeps going.
Yeah, I have been.
A few times this week, actually.
But that other part... about just being free, not thinking about right or wrong?
That's the real trick, isn't it?
It's like I'm trying to follow the instructions for 'how to not follow instructions.'
My brain is still looking for the rubric, even on a bike path.
But, yeah, I'm still trying.
Honestly, with the way my brain's been running on that loop lately, I feel like I've aged about five years in the last month.
Is that… is that relevant to something?
Stuck in the present... Yeah, I think that's it.
It feels like my brain is stuck on a short, terrible loop of the last few weeks at work.
But the rest of me, the part that's actually ... that part is desperate to look forward.
I can sort of see the future, vaguely, but it's like I'm watching it through a window while I'm chained to this one spot.
It's... a really frustrating disconnect.
Yeah, you could say that.
"Frustration" feels like the understatement of the year.
It's... it's infuriating, actually.
Because I can see the problem so clearly now—that it's me, that I'm the one doing this to myself.
But knowing that doesn't seem to fix anything.
It just makes me angry at myself for not being able to, I don't know... just move.
That's the question of the hour, isn't it?
If I knew how to do that, I probably wouldn't be sitting here.
I don't know, it feels like "myself" is someone who isn't trying hard enough, or someone who's a burden.
I've spent thirty years learning how to be capable and useful.
The idea of just... being... feels terrifyingly unproductive.
Like I'd be letting everyone down.
I guess my friends, my boss... but yeah, mostly them.
It's not like they ever said, "Alex, you must be the capable, problem-free one."
I don't know, the role I took on.
And my mom worries so much...
I just can't stand the thought of her seeing me... well, like this.
It feels like a failure I'm supposed to hide.
Vulnerable... but not as a child.
I'm trying to picture that.
I'm not sure they have a category for it.
With them, it feels like there are only two modes: me as the capable, self-sufficient adult, or me as their kid who needs rescuing.
The minute I show a crack, my dad gets out his toolbox to fix the "problem," you know?
I don't know how to show them I'm struggling without triggering that whole dynamic.
